observation_summary: The ScopedAliases pass fails to resolve aliases defined later in the scope, causing JSDoc type annotation errors. The failure occurs because the current implementation processes the AST in a single pass, lacking the necessary look-ahead or pre-scan to identify all aliases before resolving references.
hypothesis: The ScopedAliases pass performs a single-pass traversal of the AST, which prevents it from resolving aliases that are defined later in the same scope. The fix requires a two-pass approach: first to collect all alias definitions, and second to replace references to those aliases in JSDoc and code.
prediction: The ScopedAliases class will contain a single traversal method that attempts to resolve and replace aliases simultaneously, rather than separating the collection of aliases from their usage.
experiment_rationale: The failure is a classic case of an incorrect algorithmic strategy (single-pass vs. multi-pass) for resolving dependencies within a scope. The fix is to change the procedural logic of the pass to perform a pre-scan.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a procedural limitation in the ScopedAliases pass. It is not a missing check (Checking) because the logic for resolving aliases is present but incomplete; it is not an initialization error (Assignment/Initialization) because the issue is the order of operations, not the value itself. It is an Algorithm/Method defect because the traversal strategy needs to be updated to handle forward references.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a missing guard or validation, but a fundamental limitation in the traversal strategy for resolving symbols.
The fix is a local algorithmic change to the traversal logic, not a design-level change to the class structure.
